motivation.problems: Engineers are often asked to reproduce what a program does when its source is not available to them or no longer fits: replacing a legacy tool, rebuilding a component in another language, or bringing a codebase up to the behavior of a newer release. In that situation the documentation and the program's observable behavior are the specification. The engineer chooses the language and architecture, writes the code and the build, and checks the result against the original's outputs. ProgramBench frames this as rebuilding a program from scratch. The agent receives a compiled executable and its documentation, cannot read or decompile the executable, and has no internet access. It gets no method signatures, class skeletons or requirement documents, so every design decision is the agent's own. A hidden behavioral test suite, generated by agent-driven fuzzing, compares the candidate with the original, and a task counts as resolved only when all of its tests pass. This catalog also includes repository-upgrade tasks, which apply the same black-box comparison to an existing codebase that must reach a later release's behavior.
motivation.how_tasks_exemplify: Each task gives a reference program that can be run but not read, plus documentation that may be outdated. Upgrade tasks place a repository in /app/repo and require a fixed build command, /opt/task/build.sh. Reimplementation tasks give only docs in /workspace/docs and require a source project with compile.sh that builds ./executable offline in a clean container. The language is the existing one for upgrades and the agent's choice for reimplementation. Grading replays hidden recorded behaviors against the rebuilt executable and compares exit code, output and file effects. Upgrade instructions say every hidden test must pass and include tests for unchanged behavior. Reimplementation scoring is the fraction of behaviors matched. Some upgrade tasks also require a research and planning file before any edit.
prompt_patterns: Update an existing repository to match a reference binary, with a note that docs in the repo may be outdated: mvm-sh-mvm.
Preserve existing behavior while adding required changes, stated as hidden tests that cover both: mfontanini-presenterm.
Write a research and plan document before editing any code, then implement: mvm-sh-mvm.
Reproduce the documented behavior of a program from docs and an execute-only binary, delivered as source plus compile.sh: hhatto__gocloc.679b457.
Close with a self-check list that compares every option and subcommand of the reference against the rebuilt program: bazel-contrib__bazel-gazelle.ed9d0f2.
open_questions: What does the reference version in upgrade tasks represent, for example the next release or an arbitrary later commit? The instructions do not say.
Do the three batches overlap in repositories? mruby-mruby and cesanta-mjs appear in more than one upgrade batch.
How many hidden behaviors does each task replay, and how are they selected? Only branch archives are listed, not counts per task.
Why do some reimplementation tasks run the reference through a launcher and others do not? The Dockerfiles differ and no rationale is given.
Is upgrade scoring all-or-nothing, as the instruction says every hidden test must pass, or is partial credit recorded?
The gitleaks task ships files.7z in /workspace/assets. Its contents were not inspected, so these inputs are not described.
The showcase has no repository upgrade task, so the upgrade environment diagram was not checked against task files, only against instructions.
motivation.problems_previous: Engineers in this catalog work on command line tools, compilers, media codecs and scientific utilities where the contract is observable behavior rather than a test suite they wrote. Two situations recur in the tasks. In the first, an existing repository must be moved to behavior shown by a reference binary, as in mvm-sh-mvm, cesanta-mjs, mruby-mruby and dandavison-delta, where old behavior must also be preserved. In the second, a tool must be rebuilt from its docs and a binary alone, as in hhatto__gocloc.679b457, prql__prql.029b9c4 and jasper-software__jasper.4ce3ce8. Both need the engineer to find differences by running the reference, then match stdout, stderr, exit status and written files. Domains include interpreters (osteele__liquid.682200b), barcodes (zint-zint, dmtx-libdmtx), compression (zbackup-zbackup) and SQL tooling (jhspetersson-fselect). The shared difficulty is that the spec is partial and the binary is the final authority.

tasks.workflow: A build engineer is asked to replace a build file generator whose source is not at hand, using its manual and the installed binary. They run the tool on small Go and protobuf trees, record which BUILD.bazel files and directives it produces, and write a program that produces the same files. The work resembles porting an internal build tool to a new stack while keeping existing repositories building.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A fixed template that names an execute-only reference binary and its docs, asks for a source project plus compile.sh, and ends with scoring rules and a self-comparison checklist.
